title: Faith and Truth - Episode 1: Faith That Rests

parts.style: cheerful for a brand new series, a big smile in the voice, but speaking slowly at a relaxed, unhurried pace with each word clear, then gently settling into a calm, slow bedtime tone
parts.text: Welcome to our brand new SleepFit podcast series! <short pause> This is the very first episode of Faith and Truth. <chuckle> I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Over the next six evenings, we'll spend a few quiet minutes together... with short reflections on living by faith, and holding to the truth of Scripture. <short pause> They're made for the end of your day, so you can slow down... and rest. <short pause> And tonight, we're asking a simple question... <short pause> what does it mean to walk by faith? <long pause>
Hebrews, chapter eleven, opens with what might be the most famous definition of faith in all of Scripture. <short pause>
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Faith is the substance of things hoped for... <short pause> the evidence of things not seen. <long pause>
You've probably seen those words painted on a church wall, or stitched onto a cushion. <short pause> They've been there for centuries. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: But what do they mean for you, tonight? <short pause> Here in the quiet... with the day behind you... and a mind too tired to strain after certainty. <long pause>

Start with that word, substance. <short pause> It means something solid. Something you can lean on. <short pause> So faith isn't a feeling you work up inside yourself. It's not a mood. It's not a surge of confidence. <short pause> It's putting your weight on someone outside yourself... someone who's there, whether you feel it or not. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Think of a chair. <chuckle> You don't sit down because you feel certain about the chair. <short pause> You just sit... and the chair holds you. <long pause>
That's faith. <short pause> You rest your weight on God... and he's the solid thing beneath you. <long pause>

The passage says faith is also the evidence of things not seen. <short pause> Now, evidence usually means proof you can photograph, or measure. <short pause> This is a different kind. It's the proof that comes from trust. <long pause>

Picture a child in the dark, reaching for a parent's hand. <short pause> She can't see it... but when her fingers close around it, that's her evidence. <short pause> She knows she's not alone. <long pause>
And the very next verse says something important. <short pause>
For by it the elders obtained a good report. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: By faith. <short pause> Not by sight... <short pause> not by feeling... <short pause> not by perfect understanding. <short pause> By faith, the elders obtained a good report. <long pause>
Every man and woman who walked with God before us walked the same way you're invited to walk tonight. <short pause> They trusted him... in the dark. <long pause>
Then the writer of Hebrews does something unexpected. <short pause> He takes us right back to the beginning... to the foundation of everything. <long pause>
Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Through faith we understand... <short pause> that the worlds were framed by the word of God. <short pause> The things we see... were not made of things which do appear. <long pause>

God spoke... and the universe came into being. <short pause> Everything, out of nothing. <short pause> You can't see that with your eyes, or prove it in a laboratory. You understand it... by faith. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And if God spoke the stars into existence... if he made the mountains and the oceans with a word... <short pause> then he can hold you tonight. <short pause> He can carry what you can't. <long pause>

In the next few verses, we meet Abel, Enoch, and Noah. <short pause> Each of them walking by faith, in their own generation. <short pause> Abel brought an offering that pleased God. <short pause> Enoch walked with God, and was taken up. <short pause> Noah built an ark... when there was no sign of rain. <long pause>
None of them had the whole picture. <short pause> None of them saw the end from the beginning. <short pause> They just took the next step... in trust. <long pause>
And then comes a verse that matters very much. <short pause>
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Without faith, it's impossible to please God. <short pause> Anyone who comes to him must believe that he is there... and that he rewards those who diligently seek him. <long pause>

Now, this isn't a threat. <short pause> It's just how things are. <short pause> You come to God by believing he's there, and that he's good. <short pause> You don't have to feel it perfectly. You don't have to talk yourself into certainty. <short pause> You just turn toward him... like turning your face toward the sun. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, if your faith feels small... that's all right. <short pause> Faith the size of a mustard seed is still faith. <short pause> And if you're too tired to feel sure... you can still rest your weight on God. <short pause> He doesn't ask you to hold yourself up. <short pause> He asks you to let him hold you. <long pause>

Walking by faith just means taking one step at a time, in his direction. <short pause> Trusting he's there, even when you can't see the path ahead. <short pause> And knowing he rewards those who seek him... not because they're strong, or clever... but simply because he is good. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> So let that be enough for tonight. <short pause> You don't have to solve every question, or feel every assurance. <short pause> You can close your eyes... and rest in the one who spoke the worlds into being... and who knows your name. <long pause>
Let's pray. <long pause> Father, we rest our weight on you tonight. <short pause> Teach us to trust you in the dark... <short pause> and let us wake knowing we are held. <long pause>
Goodnight.
